description_en: This Stone (Ḍhuṅge) Fountain (Dhārā), built between the 14th and 16th centuries on the western slope of the main Dullu hill, is now accessible via a motorable path that departs from Dullu's central area. The Fountain is located a few metres north of the Śrī Vijayā Mādhyamika Vidyālaya (or Śrī Vijayā Highschool) and about 300 metres south of Rānāvāḍā Stone Fountain (DLK0390), and faces north. It, like most Karnali monuments of this type, has a central panel carved with pilasters and a horizontal frieze ofāmalakamotif. Water is dispensed through two stylized makara heads (only the right one was operational at the time the site was surveyed in 2022 CE). Each side of the central panel has a small platform. A flight of cement steps from the high school leads directly to the Fountain's western side. Similar fountains, known locally asmugrāhā, can be found throughout the region (Andolfatto 2019: 101-102). Given that a similar fountain found nearby was built in 1568 CE (DLK0370), it is possible to speculate that this Fountain was constructed between the 14th and 16th centuries, corresponding to the late period of the Khaśa Malla regime (12th-14th century) and the succeeding Rāskoṭi dynasty.Dhārāis a Nepālī term for fountains that is commonly used in western Nepal.Mugrāhāis another vernacular term.
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université.
